body:
## E1 step 9: the return to view-only (C half) is now observed through an entry that actually exists on the candidate line

**A correction to the earlier record first.** Comment `5731595341` reported the A and B halves using the showcase's application-wide `Ctrl+I` entry, which arrives with PR #160 - and **PR #160 is not on this candidate line**: `examples/remote-support-showcase/main.cpp` at `cc1adca` exposes only `port`, `remote-input`, `auto-start` and `seconds`. That reading was therefore taken against a tree that is not the candidate. The C half below is taken on a payload **built from `cc1adca`**, with an entry that exists there.

**Entry used**: Windows UI Automation - the element found by name `Allow remote control`, toggled through `TogglePattern`. That is the same path a mouse click on the checkbox takes: not a keyboard shortcut, not a test-only command-line option. The application confirmed the change itself by printing `REMOTE_INPUT disabled`.

**Run configuration**: `hyremote-remote-support-showcase` built from `cc1adca` out-of-tree (Ninja + `mingw1310_64` + Qt 6.8.3 `mingw_64`, Release), launched as `--port 5963 --remote-input --auto-start` so control mode is active **before** any viewer attaches. Two independent criteria are counted per session, because this payload's pointer line needs a button event: a key (`keyPress('a')`) and a pointer press (`mouseMove` + `mouseDown(1)` + `mouseUp(1)` at 200,150) - the same calls the repository's own `rfb_product_fit.py:276-278` uses, and the same methods vncdotool 1.3.0 actually exposes.

| Half | Observed | Reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B - control mode delivers | the same actions produced `SHOWCASE_KEY key=65` x3 and `SHOWCASE_POINTER x=200 y=150` x2 | control mode delivers remote input, agreed by both criteria |
| local toggle back to view-only | `ToggleState On -> Off`, then the application printed `REMOTE_INPUT disabled` followed by `REMOTE_STARTED 5963` | the policy change took effect through the real control, and the payload restarted remote access - its documented behaviour on every policy change |
| C - view-only blocks again | a fresh viewer produced `SHOWCASE_CLIENTS 1` (it really connected) and **zero** `SHOWCASE_KEY` / `SHOWCASE_POINTER` lines; the entire post-toggle log is 7 lines and contains no delivery line at all | view-only blocked remote input again, agreed by both criteria |

The contrast is what carries the claim: identical viewer actions, identical payload and configuration - delivered 3 keys and 2 pointer presses in control mode, delivered nothing after the policy returned to view-only, while still accepting the connection.

**My instrument defect, disclosed.** The first C-half script compared against a `state.json` written by an **earlier application instance** whose log had been recreated, and reported `delta KEY=-6, POINTER=-4` - meaningless numbers produced by state crossing an application restart. The criterion was corrected to per-instance log counts, which is what the table above uses. Counters must never carry across a restart of the process being measured.

**Still owed, stated plainly rather than papered over:**

- The **A half** (startup policy is view-only) was recorded earlier with the `Ctrl+I` entry, so it is not candidate-anchored either. Re-taking it on the candidate line is prepared - same payload, launched without `--remote-input`, same viewer actions - but the local process launch is currently blocked on an approval prompt that keeps timing out, so it is **not** claimed here.
- The **held-state balance** across the transition is still unobserved on this payload (no key probe; adding one to the frozen candidate was declined).
- **E2/E3 disable paths** and the **DPR interaction** cell remain open; DPR needs a scaled or multi-display host.

Refs #148
